ev.q: During 2006–2015, 79% of U.S. isolates from typhoid fever patients who traveled to Pakistan were fluoroquinolone nonsusceptible.
Fluoroquinolone nonsusceptibility increased from 55% (177 of 323 isolates) in 2006 to 66% (221 of 336) in 2015.
Of 169 isolates from travelers to Pakistan, 133 (79%) were fluoroquinolone nonsusceptible and 85 (50%) were MDR
including 244 (7%) who traveled to only Pakistan in the 30 days before onset (median = 23 patients annually)
Among these, 2,350 (65%) were fluoroquinolone nonsusceptible, 418 (12%) were MDR, and none had resistance to ceftriaxone.
Surveillance data from NARMS and NTPFS from 2006–2015 were compared with data from 2016–2018
